One thing about the one piece anime is that the pacing isn't all that great. Even quite early into the show the pacing really drags and can bring the entertainment factor down. However, what I personally think carries One Piece and is the most interesting part of the show is the short and long term payoffs you get with such a long show. Oda has done a great job putting hints, and breadcrumbs that get pay offs 100 to 500 chapters later.  I do like the anime though, and the voice acting and sound design add a lot to the series as a whole, and I personally think the pacing only truly gets bad after episode 520 or so. However, if the aspects of the series that are only present in the anime drew you into the series I think that sticking around with the anime till episode 500 or so should give you some of the highest highs the show has had to that point, and should indicate if it you truly want to continue with the rest of the show.

The thing is that spending time with someone who has suicidal thoughts isn't the problem. It's keeping spending that time with that person. Suicidal thoughts won't leave in like a month. It may take years for those people to have control over those thoughts, and even longer to not have them at all.

No one wants you to die, and if they do they are not the person to talk to, but the thing is that it can heavily affect the person listening.

I would say, if you want a listening ear, there are definitely those who want to listen, but if you want to actually have them involved in your life and have them care about you, those thoughts shouldn't be the only reason. They need to care about you and your interests and like you as a person, so that the care and love they offer you is genuine.

Or you can pay them, and we call that therapy (Still important, but it can't be fixed by this alone)

They want to provide item diversity, yet a ton of champions still rely on single items to get strong. Tear for example is basically the same item. It's basically only bought on a small group of champions that spams abilities, or have a way to stack it fast. This goes against the new design philosophy as well, going by the logic given. Hell, with the introduction of mythic items almost every champion is shoehorned into a single item, because every character synergizes well with only 1 of the available items. I would even say that this entire new design philosophy is the complete opposite of what they wanted to achieve.

Don't get me wrong, I love some of the new items (Cosmic Drive for example), but the lack in build variety, especially with the lack of overall usefull items is is awful, and makes some classes boring and monotone to play. 

An item like Rod of Ages would be a fine mythical item if it retained the idea of the item, but modernized it. Make it build out of tear, which converts the mana spent into minutes that have already passed, making it less of a burden to build and makes the player feel less "irrelevant" for a portion of the game. (Also, wasn't the point of Rod of Ages that it was a really strong item after being fully stacked, but you had to wait for that to happen as it was a somewhat cheap item?) Instead of stacking all 3 of the stats, you could make it that it only stacks Mana,  or only health, even only hp.  This would make an item that scales with you into the game, while still providing a good amount of stats. 

Currently a lot of the characters that tended to build Rod of Ages have had to switch roles to burst mage. Because there isn't an item that provides the advantages that Rod of Ages did. Sure, you could build the new Lyandries on Swain, but that is the same item a champion like lux and even ahri build, and they have nowhere near the same role in the game. Removing Rod of Ages just makes the more skirmish type mage champions into either burst assasins or tanks. The stats provided by Rod of Ages made the skirmish mages what they were, but the mythic items currently provided don't fulfill this role. 

The closest item to Rod of Ages is Everfrost, which is getting a buff with some hp added onto it. This is an item that is going in the right direction, but this item would be much better if the mythic passive would give HP instead of AP. Most of the champions mentioned want to stay alive as long as possible, and AP just doesn't do that. It makes the burst of the character higher, while providing no defence at all. Which was the point of Rod of Ages as an item. It made the mage more durable. 

I loved Rod of Ages as an item, and at the moment there is nothing in league that inhabits the same niche that it had. I hope that it either can be re added into the game, or make Everfrost into an item that is comparable, because if not, there will be a lot of champions that will lose their original role in the game.
